summary: Bradford's Instagram record on social services spans homelessness, mental health, public health, recreation, seniors, community/diversity, and reconciliation. Bradford supports encampment clearance paired with offering shelter and treatment, and states the province should fund addiction and mental health as health care issues (DTu89cQjtBR, DRCZSYbjSpb, DSZ7R5JgJZS). Bradford supports expanded mental health outreach, shelters, supportive housing, and youth programs (DMK2uOQgteh, Cs6kSzKgQxQ, DaL1nWGKEEM). During COVID-19, Bradford promoted vaccination access in hot-spot neighbourhoods and City employee vaccine requirements (CNctisNh0X6, CSwreCcrT6v). Bradford supports arts funding, food security programs, refugee welcoming with federal funding, seniors' Meals on Wheels and community paramedicine, and Indigenous reconciliation (DCX1fRQNc0a, CtW8t0Pp_Ix, CVd490bgrii, CcBq_fmLPzw). Bradford opposes the current 7am recreation registration system and pledges a lottery-based replacement (DZIQEviO7nH). Bradford consistently expresses solidarity with 2SLGBTQ+, Jewish, Muslim, Tamil, Black, and trans communities.

key_positions.stance: Supports clearing encampments while offering shelter and treatment options, framing it as a compassionate approach
States addiction and mental health are provincial health care jurisdictions and the province must step in to help municipalities
Supports more shelters, supportive housing, mental health supports, and supports for people struggling with addiction
Supports federal funding for refugee support programs, noting refugees and asylum seekers make up roughly 40% of Toronto's shelter population
Supports targeted COVID-19 vaccination in hot-spot neighbourhoods and City employee vaccine requirements
Supports Toronto arts sector funding through the Culture Plan, TAC, and LASOs
Supports food security programs including food banks, Out of the Cold, and Meals on Wheels
Opposes Toronto's current 7am recreation program registration process and supports a longer registration window with a fair lottery
Supports affordable and accessible daycare as critical to children and the economy
Supports Truth and Reconciliation with Indigenous peoples, including the City's Reconciliation Action Plan
Supports 2SLGBTQ+ communities and opposes homophobia, biphobia, and transphobia
Supports Jewish, Muslim, Tamil, and Ukrainian communities and opposes antisemitism, Islamophobia, and hate
Opposes changing the provincial definition of disability, calling it inhumane to further pressure people already struggling
Supports seniors' services including Meals on Wheels, community paramedicine, snow removal supports, and Aging in Place
